subject: World History: Modern

topics.title: 1.1 Developments in East Asia from c. 1200 to c. 1450

subtopics.title: Developments in East Asia from c. 1200 to c. 1450

outcomes.text: Explain how the Song dynasty used Confucian tradition and bureaucracy to rule, and how 13th-century states showed continuity and innovation.
Describe how Chinese cultural traditions persisted and influenced neighboring regions.
Describe how Buddhism and its branches kept shaping Asian societies.
Explain how Song China's economy grew commercial yet still relied on free peasant and artisan labor.
Explain how Song China's economy flourished through farming and manufacturing innovation and wider trade.

topics.title: 1.2 Developments in Dar al-Islam from c. 1200 to c. 1450

subtopics.title: Developments in Dar al-Islam from c. 1200 to c. 1450

outcomes.text: Describe how Islam, Judaism and Christianity shaped societies in Africa and Asia.
Explain how new, mostly Turkic-led Islamic states emerged as the Abbasid Caliphate fragmented.
Explain how Muslim rule and Islam spread through conquest, merchants, missionaries and Sufis.
Explain how Muslim states encouraged intellectual innovation and transfer of knowledge.

topics.title: 1.3 Developments in South and Southeast Asia from c. 1200 to c. 1450

subtopics.title: Developments in South and Southeast Asia from c. 1200 to c. 1450

outcomes.text: Describe how Hinduism, Islam and Buddhism shaped South and Southeast Asian societies.
Explain how new Hindu and Buddhist states formed in South and Southeast Asia.
Explain how American states showed continuity, innovation and growing reach.
Explain how African states showed continuity, innovation and growing reach.

topics.title: 1.6 Developments in Europe from c. 1200 to c. 1450

subtopics.title: Developments in Europe from c. 1200 to c. 1450

outcomes.text: Describe how Christianity, Judaism and Islam shaped European societies.
Explain how Europe's decentralized monarchies, feudalism and manorialism fragmented power.
Explain how Europe's farming economy relied on free and coerced labor, including serfdom.

topics.title: 1.7 Comparison in the Period from c. 1200 to c. 1450

subtopics.title: Comparison in the Period from c. 1200 to c. 1450

outcomes.text: Compare how states formed and developed in different regions with continuity, innovation and diversity.
Explain how better commercial practices expanded trade and trading cities along the Silk Roads.
Explain how caravanserai, credit and money economies boosted luxury trade.
Explain how rising demand for luxury goods expanded Chinese, Persian and Indian textile, porcelain and iron production.

topics.title: 2.2 The Mongol Empire and the Making of the Modern World

subtopics.title: The Mongol Empire and the Making of the Modern World

outcomes.text: Explain how empires collapsed and Mongol khanates replaced them in places.
Explain how Mongol expansion helped trade and communication across Afro-Eurasia.
Explain how contacts and conflicts, including Mongol ones, spread technology and culture.
Explain how better transport and commerce expanded Indian Ocean trade and trading cities.
Explain how compass, astrolabe and bigger ships boosted trade.
Explain how the Indian Ocean network helped states grow.
Describe merchant diaspora communities and cultural blending along trade routes.
Describe cultural and technology transfers, including Zheng He's maritime voyages.
Explain how monsoon knowledge enabled long-distance trade.
Explain how transport innovations encouraged interregional trade.
Explain how the trans-Saharan network expanded trade.
Explain how Mali's expansion supported trade and communication.
Explain how cross-cultural contact spread art, literature, science and technology.
Explain how cities rose and declined with productivity and trade.
Describe how growing exchange led more travelers to write about their journeys.
Explain how crops and pathogens such as the bubonic plague spread along trade routes.
Compare how deeper exchange networks spread culture, technology and disease across societies.
Explain how changing trade networks raised productive capacity and affected social, gender and environmental patterns.
Explain how gunpowder, cannons and armed trade enabled large empires in both hemispheres.
Identify the Manchu, Mughal, Ottoman and Safavid land empires.
Explain how political and religious disputes caused rivalries between states.
Describe rulers' use of bureaucratic elites and military professionals to centralize control.
Describe rulers' use of religion, art and monumental architecture to legitimize rule.
Describe tribute, tax farming and new taxes as ways to fund state expansion.
Explain how the Protestant and Catholic reformations grew Christianity and broke tradition.
Explain how Ottoman-Safavid rivalry deepened the Sunni-Shi'a split.
Explain how Sikhism developed between Hinduism and Islam.
Explain how transoceanic voyaging linked the hemispheres and changed trade and society.
Explain how new contacts spread religions, caused conflict and produced syncretic beliefs.
Compare how empires gained reach and were shaped by the peoples they absorbed.
Explain how knowledge and technology from Classical, Islamic and Asian worlds fed European innovation.
Describe new tools, ship designs and wind and current knowledge that enabled ocean trade.

topics.title: 4.2 Exploration: Causes and Events from 1450 to 1750

subtopics.title: Exploration: Causes and Events from 1450 to 1750

outcomes.text: Describe state-supported transoceanic exploration.
Explain how Portuguese navigation built a global trading-post empire.
Explain how Spanish sponsorship of Columbus and later voyages increased interest in ocean trade.
Explain how English, French and Dutch Atlantic crossings sought new routes to Asia.
Describe the Columbian Exchange of plants, animals and diseases between hemispheres.
Explain how disease transfer devastated indigenous American populations.
Explain how American foods became staples abroad and cash crops grew on coerced-labor plantations.
Describe Old World crops and animals brought to the Americas by Europeans and enslaved Africans.
Explain how American crops improved nutrition in Afro-Eurasia.
Explain how European trading posts profited rulers and how some Asian states restricted trade.
Explain how rivalries led European states to build maritime empires.
Explain how Indian Ocean trade kept thriving despite European arrivals.
Describe colonial American agricultural economies and their old and new labor systems.
Describe continued forms of enslavement in Africa and exports of enslaved people to Mediterranean and Indian Ocean regions.
Explain how plantation growth raised demand for enslaved labor in the Americas and reshaped societies.
Explain how mercantilism and joint-stock companies helped rulers expand and compete.
Explain how economic disputes caused rivalry and conflict between states.
Explain gender and family restructuring, including demographic change in Africa from the slave trade.
Explain how the Atlantic system mixed African, American and European cultures.
Explain how the Atlantic system moved goods, wealth and enslaved labor.
Explain how monopoly companies and silver flows created a global circulation of goods.
Describe continued peasant and artisan labor amid rising demand.

topics.title: 4.6 Internal and External Challenges to State Power from 1450 to 1750

subtopics.title: Internal and External Challenges to State Power from 1450 to 1750

outcomes.text: Explain how state centralization provoked local resistance.
Describe organized resistance by enslaved people in the Americas.
Explain how states accommodated or suppressed ethnic and religious diversity.
Explain how conquest and global trade created new elites, such as under the Qing and the Casta system.
Explain how elite power shifted against stronger monarchs.
Explain changes in labor, manufacturing, gender, social structure and environment in an agricultural world.
Explain how global demand for raw materials intensified labor, plantations and the Atlantic slave trade.
Describe Enlightenment reason, empiricism and new political ideas about individuals and natural rights.
Explain how Enlightenment thought preceded revolutions against existing governments.
Explain how nationalism shaped states and empires.
Explain how Enlightenment and religious ideals drove reforms like suffrage, abolition and the end of serfdom.
Explain how women's suffrage demands and early feminism challenged hierarchies.

topics.title: 5.2 Nationalism and Revolutions in the Period from 1750 to 1900

subtopics.title: Nationalism and Revolutions in the Period from 1750 to 1900

outcomes.text: Explain how language, religion, customs and territory built shared identity used by governments.
Explain how revolutions and rebellions from the 18th century created new nation-states.
Explain how discontent with monarchy and empire fostered democracy and liberalism.
Describe American, Haitian, French and Latin American revolutions and their influence.
Identify Enlightenment ideas in revolutionary documents.
Explain how national identity became tied to state borders and unification or boundary challenges.
List factors that enabled the Industrial Revolution, such as waterways, coal and iron, urbanization and farm productivity.
Explain how factories concentrated production and increased specialization.

topics.title: 5.4 Industrialization Spreads in the Period from 1750 to 1900

subtopics.title: Industrialization Spreads in the Period from 1750 to 1900

outcomes.text: Explain how steam-powered industry raised Europe's and the U.S.'s share of global manufacturing.
Explain how industrial methods spread to other parts of Europe, the U.S., Russia and Japan.
Explain how steam and combustion engines unlocked fossil fuel energy.
Describe the second industrial revolution in steel, chemicals, electricity and machinery.
Explain how railroads, steamships and the telegraph opened interiors and increased trade and migration.
Explain how some states promoted state-sponsored industrialization.
Explain how Meiji Japan's reforms supported industrialization and regional power.

topics.title: 5.7 Economic Developments and Innovations in the Industrial Age

subtopics.title: Economic Developments and Innovations in the Industrial Age

outcomes.text: Explain the shift from mercantilism to free trade and laissez-faire ideas.
Explain how global trade produced transnational businesses and new banking practices.
Explain how industrial capitalism raised living standards for some and expanded consumer goods.

topics.title: 5.8 Reactions to the Industrial Economy from 1750 to 1900

subtopics.title: Reactions to the Industrial Economy from 1750 to 1900

outcomes.text: Describe reform movements responding to industrial capitalism.
Describe labor unions and workers' movements seeking better conditions.
Explain how discontent fostered socialism, communism and Marx's ideas.
Describe Ottoman and Qing reform and modernization efforts and resistance to them.
Describe new social classes, the middle class and industrial working class.
Explain changing roles of women and children across classes.
Explain problems of rapid urbanization: pollution, poverty, crime and health crises.
Explain how Social Darwinism, nationalism, the civilizing mission and religious conversion justified imperialism.
Explain how states tightened control over existing colonies.
Explain how Europe, the U.S. and Japan acquired territory in Asia and the Pacific.
Explain how European states used war and diplomacy to expand in Africa.
Describe European settler colonies.
Describe U.S., Russian and Japanese expansion over neighboring lands.

topics.title: 6.3 Indigenous Responses to State Expansion from 1750 to 1900

subtopics.title: Indigenous Responses to State Expansion from 1750 to 1900

outcomes.text: Explain how questions of authority and nationalism fueled anticolonial movements.
Describe forms of anti-imperial resistance and new peripheral states.
Explain rebellions against imperial rule, some shaped by religion.
Explain how demand for raw materials and food created export economies worldwide.
Explain economic imperialism by industrialized states in Asia and Latin America.
Explain how some commodity trades favored European and U.S. firms.

topics.title: 6.6 Causes of Migration in an Interconnected World

subtopics.title: Causes of Migration in an Interconnected World

outcomes.text: Explain how demographic change drove migration in industrial and nonindustrial societies.
Explain how new transport moved migrants to cities and allowed return and urbanization.
Describe voluntary migration in search of work.
Describe coerced and semicoerced labor migration such as indentured servitude and convict labor.
Explain how male migration changed women's roles at home.
Describe ethnic enclaves that carried culture abroad.
Explain prejudice and state efforts to regulate immigration.
Explain how industrializing states expanded empires and created new overseas relationships.
Explain how empires and global capitalism changed migration patterns.
Explain how Western dominance gave way to new states as empires ended.
Explain how the Ottoman, Russian and Qing empires collapsed, leading to communist revolution in Russia.
Describe challenges to the political and social order such as the Mexican Revolution.
Explain how imperialism, regional conflicts, alliances and nationalism caused World War I.
Explain how World War I became total war with propaganda and mobilization.
Explain how new military technology raised casualties.
Explain how governments took a bigger role in the economy after World War I and the Great Depression.
Explain how Soviet Five Year Plans controlled the economy with repressive effects.

topics.title: 7.5 Unresolved Tensions After World War I

subtopics.title: Unresolved Tensions After World War I

outcomes.text: Explain how imperial powers held or expanded colonies between the wars amid resistance.
Explain how the peace settlement, Great Depression, imperial ambitions and fascism caused World War II.
Explain how World War II was total war using propaganda, ideology and mobilization.
Explain how new weapons and tactics, including the atomic bomb, raised casualties.
Explain how extremist rule led to the Holocaust and other genocides and ethnic violence.
Explain how rapid scientific and technological advances changed communication, industry, agriculture and medicine.
Explain how peoples and states challenged the existing order, causing worldwide conflicts.

topics.title: 8.1 Setting the Stage for the Cold War and Decolonization

subtopics.title: Setting the Stage for the Cold War and Decolonization

outcomes.text: Explain how unfulfilled self-government hopes and anti-imperialism dissolved empires after World War II.
Explain how World War II gains by victors shifted the global balance of power.
Explain how the U.S. and USSR became superpowers in an ideological struggle.
Describe movements, like the Non-Aligned Movement, offering alternatives to the existing order.
Describe NATO, the Warsaw Pact, nuclear proliferation and proxy wars.
Explain how internal tension and Japanese aggression brought communists to power in China.
Explain how Chinese state control, as in the Great Leap Forward, had repressive costs.
Describe nationalist leaders seeking autonomy or independence in Asia and Africa.
Contrast negotiated independence with independence won by armed struggle.
Explain regional, religious and ethnic movements against colonial rule and inherited borders.
Explain how redrawn boundaries created new states.
Explain how boundary changes caused conflict and displacement, as in India's Partition and Israel.
Explain how new states' governments often led economic development.
Explain how migration to former colonizers kept cultural and economic ties.

topics.title: 8.7 Global Resistance to Established Power Structures After 1900

subtopics.title: Global Resistance to Established Power Structures After 1900

outcomes.text: Describe individuals, groups and states that opposed conflict and others that intensified it.
Describe nonviolent resistance by Gandhi, King and Mandela.
Explain how militarized states escalated conflicts.
Describe movements using violence against civilians.
Explain how U.S. advances, the Afghanistan invasion and communist discontent ended the Cold War.

topics.title: 8.9 Causation in the Age of the Cold War and Decolonization

subtopics.title: Causation in the Age of the Cold War and Decolonization

outcomes.text: Explain how the Cold War shaped economic, political, social and cultural events worldwide.
Explain how states' economic roles varied and global institutions emerged.
Explain how states responded to 20th-century economic challenges.

topics.title: 9.1 Advances in Technology and Exchange After 1900

subtopics.title: Advances in Technology and Exchange After 1900

outcomes.text: Explain how communication and transport advances shrank distance.
Explain how petroleum and nuclear energy raised production.
Explain how birth control gave women fertility control and lowered fertility rates.
Explain how the Green Revolution and commercial agriculture sustained population growth.
Explain how vaccines and antibiotics lengthened lives.

topics.title: 9.2 Technological Advances and Limitations After 1900: Disease

subtopics.title: Technological Advances and Limitations After 1900: Disease

outcomes.text: Explain how diseases and medical advances affected world populations.
Describe persistent poverty diseases, new epidemics and the technological responses they spurred.

topics.title: 9.3 Technological Advances: Debates About the Environment After 1900

subtopics.title: Technological Advances: Debates About the Environment After 1900

outcomes.text: Explain how deforestation, air and water pressures intensified competition for resources.
Explain how greenhouse gases fueled debates on climate change.
Explain how governments promoted free markets after the Cold War.
Explain how information technology grew knowledge economies and moved manufacturing to Asia and Latin America.
Explain how multinational firms and trade agreements spread free-market practices.

topics.title: 9.5 Calls for Reform and Responses After 1900

subtopics.title: Calls for Reform and Responses After 1900

outcomes.text: Explain how rights-based ideas challenged assumptions about race, class, gender and religion.
Explain how education and political roles became more inclusive.
Describe protests against unequal effects of global integration.
Explain how arts changed and popular and consumer culture globalized.
Explain how arts and entertainment reflected globalization.
Explain how consumer culture crossed national borders.
Describe varied responses to cultural and economic globalization.

topics.title: 9.8 Institutions Developing in a Globalized World

subtopics.title: Institutions Developing in a Globalized World

outcomes.text: Describe new international organizations such as the UN for peace and cooperation.
